artists.biography:
The Cure are an English alternative rock band formed in Crawley, West Sussex in 1976. The band has experienced several line-up changes, with frontman, vocalist, guitarist and principal songwriter Robert Smith being the only constant member. The Cure first began releasing music in the late 1970s with its debut album Three Imaginary Boys (1979); this, along with several early singles, placed the band as part of the post-punk and New Wave movements that had sprung up in the wake of the punk rock revolution in the United Kingdom. During the early 1980s, the band's increasingly dark and tormented music helped form the gothic rock genre.

After the release of Pornography (1982), the band's future was uncertain and Smith was keen to move past the gloomy reputation his band had acquired. With the 1982 single "Let's Go to Bed" Smith began to place a pop sensibility into the band's music (as well as a unique stage look). The Cure's popularity increased as the decade wore on, especially in the United States where the songs "Just Like Heaven", "Lovesong" and "Friday I'm in Love" entered the Billboard Hot 100 chart. By the start of the 1990s, The Cure were one of the most popular alternative rock bands in the world. The band is estimated to have sold 27 million albums as of 2004. The Cure have released thirteen studio albums, 10 EPs and over thirty singles during the course of their career. Since 2010, they have been working on a fourteenth studio album.

perplexity.description:
Songs of a Lost World is the Cure's fourteenth studio album, released in November 2024 after a sixteen-year hiatus from studio recording. Marking the band's first full-length album to feature guitarist Reeves Gabrels as a permanent member since 2012, the record represents a significant return for the British rock institution. Notably, all songs on the album were written solely by frontman Robert Smith, distinguishing it from previous Cure releases. The album achieved immediate commercial success, debuting at number one on the UK charts—ending a 32-year gap since the band's last chart-topping album—and topping charts across multiple European territories including France, Germany, Sweden, and the Netherlands. It was certified as 2024's best-selling new vinyl release by a British artist and earned Grammy nominations alongside three BRIT Award nominations.

Songs of a Live World: Troxy London MMXXIV documents the album's launch performance, recorded on November 1, 2024, at London's Troxy venue before 3,000 fans. Released in December 2024, this live album captures the band performing the new record in its entirety for the first and only time, followed by an extensive set of classic material spanning their four-decade career. A cinema film version, directed by Grammy-nominated Nick Wickham and remixed by Robert Smith, was released in December 2024 as a limited theatrical engagement, presenting the 31-song performance in 4K remastered format with new surround sound. The live documentation underscores the album's significance as a major artistic statement and commercial event for one of rock's most enduring and influential acts.
